## Motivation

Fixes #43413 for the Triton Mamba2 prefill path.

A request can land on a different physical scan chunk depending on its neighbors. Chunked prefill and prefix-cache reuse can also resume from a state produced by a different floating-point computation. The request's chunk grid and its cached checkpoints both need to stay consistent.

## Modifications

- Give each request a canonical chunk grid within one padded scan. Carry CPU boundaries through prefill metadata to avoid a device-to-host sync in each layer.
- Align truncated prefill by its absolute end position and preserve the scheduler's request-slot admission check.
- Use canonical scan states as deterministic prefill checkpoints. Round FP16/BF16 boundary states before continuing the recurrence, so a resumed scan reads the same precision as an unsplit one.
- Keep boundary-state copies separate from the varlen matrix reduction to avoid the gfx950 compiler assertion reported in review. Return final states from the scan itself, including after zero-dt padding, instead of recomputing partial tails. A single request copies its final state directly.
- Keep decode and speculative verification from promoting recurrent states to prefill checkpoints. With `no_buffer`, donate only aligned, unfinished prefill states. Restrict this policy to models that use the Mamba2 SSD scan.
- Clear the preceding sequence's contribution to positive zero before the local dot. The signed-zero case reproduced on W7900D with the original PR.
- Cover mixed batches, split states, optional scan arguments, checkpoint extraction, scheduling and cache reuse.

NGRAM tree/stream fixes and FlashInfer dependency experiments remain separate contributions.

## Accuracy Tests

### Follow-up for the MI350X review

The follow-up in `3d99406c` is based on `dc63e803`. The final sources have compiler and W7900D operator coverage, plus fresh 4090D operator and Granite serving coverage. MI350X execution of the reported failures is still pending.

| Scope | Environment | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Related operator tests | W7900D/gfx1100, Torch 2.10.0+rocm7.1, triton-rocm 3.6.0 | 402 passed, no skips: 390 zero-tolerance cases and 12 existing tracking cases with their original tolerances. |
| Ordinary-mode comparison | Same environment, matched tuning configurations | 36 comparisons of outputs and states passed with zero tolerance. |
| Reported optional-argument case | Same environment | 64 complete-call repeats passed. |
| Large-stride copies | Same environment | Passed with a source offset of 2³¹ FP16 elements, using about 4 GiB of backing storage. |
| gfx950 compilation | Dockerfile-pinned `3.7.0+amd.rocm7.2.0.git89002410` | The published PR aborts on 18/186 recorded specializations. The follow-up compiles 186/186, plus 96/96 additional reduction/copy specializations. No gfx950 binary was executed locally. |
| CUDA sm89 compilation | Same compiler package's NVIDIA backend | Both specialization sets compile: 186/186 and 96/96. This is compilation coverage, not CUDA execution. |

The new final-state invariant compares the returned checkpoint with the scan's own terminal state. In a red/green run using the same AMD Triton 3.7 environment on both sides, the old PR fails 33/96 cases, including seven with FP16/BF16 caches; the follow-up passes all 96. The original 42 split/unsplit cases pass on the local W7900D baseline, so the five MI350X failures have not been reproduced on that hardware. They still need the tester's rerun.

The first W7900D run used AMD Triton 3.7 and found an intermittent BF16 scan-output difference. A fixed-input replay also reproduces it with the unchanged upstream scan: the 8-warp configuration differs in 1/2,048 upstream replays and 2/2,048 candidate replays. With Torch's declared Triton 3.6 dependency, neither source differs in 8,192 replays. The final operator results above use that matched environment; this does not establish behavior for every Triton build or for gfx950.

The operator loader isolates unrelated server imports while running the repository's real kernels and test assertions. It does not validate the complete serving installation. No tolerance was relaxed.

### Fresh 4090D validation of this follow-up

Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0, CUDA 13 compiler tools, sglang-kernel 0.4.9 and FlashInfer 0.7.1. The same final sources pass 766 operator cases (no failures or skips); 402 related cases also pass with normal SGLang imports. Ordinary-mode comparisons with matched tuning configurations pass all 36 cases. Large-stride access beyond the signed 32-bit element-offset range passes. Side-stream checks pass in six configurations, and the GPU-resident scan pipeline matches eager execution across 48 changed-input graph replays. Four sanitizer checks report no errors in the 12 boundary-copy cases, with API probe reporting disabled.

For Granite from ModelScope, the original 30-trial prefix test and a separate 465-response exact token/logprob comparison pass. Six configurations cover default attention, unaligned chunk size 513, FP16/BF16 SSM states, lazy caching and no_buffer: 1,152 boundary-check responses have no token/logprob differences, and all 54 decode-cache reuse cases pass. These are Granite results, not validation of Falcon-H1 or Nemotron Nano.

The checkpoint test fails 24/96 cases on the old PR on this GPU (all FP32 caches), versus 0/96 on the follow-up. The five reported MI350X failures still need the original platform's rerun. Direct graph capture of the entire mixed-prefill Python wrapper remains unsupported in both revisions because it constructs unpinned CPU metadata; that failed diagnostic is separate from the passing GPU-stage replay and serving decode-graph checks.

<details>
<summary>Earlier integration evidence — not validation of this follow-up</summary>

The following results use main at `877be2974aa151a984e52822c028276c2b1e9303`, single-device execution and ModelScope weights. Comparisons are exact within each platform, not between platforms.

| Platform / revision | Results |
| --- | --- |
| RTX 4090 D, published core at `dc63e803`; Torch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0 | 1,004 related GPU tests passed; 16 SM100-only cases skipped. Related CPU regression: 517 tests and 638 subtests passed. |
| W7900D, earlier 12-file follow-up; Torch 2.10.0+rocm7.1, Triton 3.7.0 | 438 operator tests passed. Five Granite configurations produced 960 responses with no token/logprob differences; 18 decode-cache reuse cases passed. |
| Ascend 910B2C, the same earlier follow-up; CANN 9.0, Triton Ascend 3.2.1.dev | 24 scan cases without initial states passed with zero tolerance. Initial-state compilation and model startup were blocked; this is partial coverage. |

At `dc63e803` on the 4090 D, Granite passed the original 30-trial prefix test, a separate 465-response exact comparison, and cold/warm/concurrent checks across chunk sizes 256/512/513, cache disabled, lazy and `no_buffer` strategies, FP32/BF16/FP16 SSM states, and graph/overlap settings. Long-context checks reached 8,193 prompt tokens. Ordinary-mode outputs for five small models matched clean upstream in the tested workloads.

The older W7900D model runs needed separate gfx1100 kernel-build, GEMM-pipeline and ROCm convolution-import adaptations, which are not included here. Ascend initial-state compilation also crashes on the original PR, and an existing main scan test crashes at the same compiler stage. Model startup on that stack is blocked by missing/version-mismatched NPU operators.

Earlier CUDA memory, initialization, race and synchronization checks found no errors in the tested cases with API reporting disabled. Default memcheck separately reports a Triton loader `cuFuncSetAttribute` probe error, reproduced without SGLang. One DSpark CPU file was excluded because `deep_gemm` was unavailable.

</details>

Remaining validation and related issues: stock FlashInfer has independent attention and Mamba SSU batch-dependent cases reproduced without SGLang. NGRAM requires separate tree/stream fixes, and Qwen NGRAM logprob differences remain reproducible on clean upstream. These are not passing configurations of this PR. The reported Falcon-H1 7B `sampling_seed` case and Nemotron Nano 9B have not been validated locally.

The Granite serving environment exercises the installed model path. Its package metadata check still lists nine other declared components as missing, including DeepGEMM/DeepEP, FlashAttention 4, TileLang and audio components. Full-installation validation remains pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

W7900D with the final matched runtime above, BF16 inputs, 48 heads, head width 64, state size 128, chunk size 256, no D/z/initial state. Two runs per revision in baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline order; each configuration uses warmups followed by five groups of 100 calls. The measured interval includes Python dispatch, allocation and a synchronization at the end of each group, and excludes compilation.

| Request lengths | SSM cache | Published PR / ms | Follow-up / ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 129 | FP32 | 0.3793 | 0.3146 |
| 129 | BF16 | 0.3749 | 0.3169 |
| 1,025 | FP32 | 0.3731 | 0.3125 |
| 1,025 | BF16 | 0.3715 | 0.3144 |
| 31 / 511 / 1,025 | FP32 | 1.0777 | 0.9811 |
| 31 / 511 / 1,025 | BF16 | 0.9152 | 0.8393 |

These are warmed SSD operator measurements. The same six points on 4090D show 6.7–17.0% lower wrapper latency with the follow-up, using the same alternating-run protocol. Neither result establishes model-serving throughput or MI350X performance.

<details>
<summary>Earlier model-serving benchmark at dc63e803</summary>

RTX 4090 D, Granite, 16 requests with prompt lengths 31/255/511/1025 repeated four times, 64 output tokens each; three warmups and five timed runs:

| | Clean upstream | Published core |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median elapsed time | 3.1386 s | 3.4072 s |
| Output throughput | 326.26 token/s | 300.54 token/s |

Throughput fell 7.9% on that workload. Padding/copies and more conservative checkpoint reuse have a cost. A packing-kernel prototype did not improve service throughput and regressed one tested shape, so it was not included. This historical result is not a measurement of the current follow-up.

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with the repository's formatter, lint and test-registration checks.
- [x] Add and run unit/operator regression tests.
- [x] Review documentation: existing flag behavior, no new user-facing option.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed evidence with the tested revisions and limitations.
- [x] Run the final follow-up on NVIDIA, including the split-state cases and Granite serving regression.
- [ ] Rerun the original failures on MI350X.
- [x] Rerun Granite model-serving regression for the final follow-up.
- [ ] Validate the reported Falcon-H1 sampling_seed and Nemotron Nano cases.
- [ ] Complete official CI and review.

nodes.body: @BBuf Could you add `run-ci` and rerun the current commit? The initial gate stopped at the missing label. I ran the Mamba GPU tests and the 30-trial Granite prefix reproduction on an RTX 4090; the results and a remaining cache-dependent logprob difference are in the description.

Hi @DQR-Happy. I tested this PR on AMD MI350X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.4, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261012`) with Granite 4.0-H tiny, Falcon-H1 7B and Nemotron Nano 9B v2, `--attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference`, triton everywhere. (On ROCm these models also need two small startup fixes, #44197 and #44198: `mamba.py` does not import the causal conv1d kernels on ROCm, and `ReLU2` has no ROCm path. Both were applied in both runs below.)

Same batch-size check as `test_deterministic --test-mode single`, but comparing every response's token IDs and log-probabilities with the batch-size-1 one (1,275 responses):

| Model | without the PR | with the PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Granite 4.0-H tiny | 359 / 1,275 token IDs, 99 log-probabilities identical | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Falcon-H1 7B | 397 / 99 | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Nemotron Nano 9B v2 | 1,245 / 99 | 1,275 / 1,275 |

The PR's kernel test (`test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py`) passes on MI350X: 380 passed (16 of them fail without the PR).

`--test-mode prefix` (prompts of different lengths in one batch) improves a lot (Granite distinct outputs per group 1/106/9/6 -> 1/1/2/1) but is not fully clean. On our side that comes from chunked prefill: with `--chunked-prefill-size -1`, Granite and Nemotron-H pass every mode, log-probabilities included. Aligning the chunked-prefill split to `mamba_chunk_size` (as #44076 does for Gated DeltaNet) reduces the differences but does not remove them, and storing the SSM state in fp32 (`--mamba-ssm-dtype float32`) does not change them, so a split prompt still ends up slightly different from an unsplit one; we have not tracked that down yet. Falcon-H1 also differs without chunked prefill, but only when the request carries a `sampling_seed` (which `test_deterministic` always sends), even at temperature 0.

Thanks for the PR.

@aarnetalman Thanks for testing this on MI350X and narrowing down the remaining cases. I've pushed a follow-up for chunked prefill and cache reuse.

Alignment alone was not enough: a continuation could restart from a decode-produced checkpoint, and low-precision SSM caches rounded split and unsplit scans differently. The update uses canonical scan checkpoints, aligns splits by the absolute end position, and applies the same boundary rounding in both paths. It also keeps recurrent decode/verify states out of the prefill cache.

On W7900D I reproduced a mixed-batch difference with the original PR: 12 BF16 output elements differed for a 256-token request after a 31-token neighbor. Explicitly clearing the previous sequence's accumulator to positive zero before the local dot fixed that case. I cannot yet say whether this is the cause of the residual MI350X differences you saw.

The local coverage is:

| Platform | Tested revision and result |
| --- | --- |
| RTX 4090 D | Latest core: 1,004 GPU tests passed, 16 SM100-only cases skipped. Granite's 30-trial prefix test and exact token/logprob comparisons across split-prefill, cache and low-precision-state settings passed. |
| W7900D | Earlier follow-up: 438 operator tests, 960 Granite responses across five configurations, and 18 decode-cache reuse cases passed. Model runs needed separate RDNA startup/build adaptations. |
| Ascend 910B2C | Earlier follow-up: 24 zero-tolerance scan cases without initial states passed. Initial-state compilation and model startup remain blocked on that software stack; this is not full NPU validation. |

Only the 4090 D has run the final expanded core revision. The PR description now includes these boundaries and the measured 7.9% throughput cost on the fixed Granite workload. Separate NGRAM and FlashInfer issues are documented there too.

I have not validated Nemotron Nano 9B or your Falcon-H1 7B `sampling_seed` case, so I am not claiming those are resolved. If you have time to rerun the split/unsplit and prefix checks on this revision, that would help confirm the remaining MI350X behavior.

@DQR-Happy Thanks for the new version and the detailed write-up. I reran it on MI350X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.4, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261013`, `--attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference`, with #44197 and #44198 for the ROCm startup fixes), and it doesn't run there yet:

1. **The servers abort at the first prefill.** Granite 4.0-H tiny, Falcon-H1 7B and Nemotron Nano 9B v2 all stop while Triton compiles `_chunk_state_varlen_kernel` (called from `chunk_state_varlen` in `_mamba_chunk_scan_combined_fwd`):

   ```
   llvm/include/llvm/ADT/Sequence.h:275: llvm::iota_range<unsigned int>::iota_range(T, T, bool) [T = unsigned int]:
   Assertion `Begin <= End && "Begin must be less or equal to End."' failed.
   Fatal Python error: Aborted
     File ".../triton/backends/amd/compiler.py", line 544 in make_amdgcn
     ...
     File ".../ssd_chunk_state.py", in chunk_state_varlen
     File ".../ssd_combined.py", in _mamba_chunk_scan_combined_fwd
   ```

   That kernel is the one this version changes (`final_states_ptr`, `USE_SCAN_BOUNDARIES`, the `tl.where(reuse_scan_state, 0, chunk_size_limit)` limit). The same setup without the PR serves these models (our earlier runs), so it looks like a ROCm Triton backend problem triggered by the new code path. The servers use the default chunked prefill.

2. **`test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` (the PR's version): 5 failed, 662 passed.** All five failures are in the new `test_mamba_chunk_scan_split_boundary_state`, always with `with_initial_state=False` and an fp16 or bf16 `state_dtype`. The failing assertion is the last split segment's final state against the unsplit scan's (`assert_close(full[2], partial[2], atol=0, rtol=0)`): 4-6 of 393,216 elements, max abs diff 6.1e-5 to 2.0e-3. Which parameter sets fail changes between runs (first run: at least four of the five with fp16 states; rerunning only this test: one fp16 and four bf16), so on this GPU the split and unsplit final states are not reproducible run to run in low precision. The other new tests (`test_mamba_batch_invariant.py`, `test_mamba_chunk_alignment.py`, `test_mamba_deterministic_checkpoints.py`, `test_mamba_prefill_track_metadata.py`) pass.

One more thing to coordinate: this version aligns chunked-prefill splits on absolute positions in the scheduler, the same lines my #44076 changes for Gated DeltaNet (Qwen3.5/3.8) chunk alignment. Whichever merges first, the other will need a rebase, and it would be good to end up with one alignment rule for both mamba and GDN layers. Happy to adapt #44076 to yours.

I can rerun as soon as there's a new version, including Nemotron Nano 9B v2 and the Falcon-H1 `sampling_seed` case.

@aarnetalman Thanks for the detailed report and for offering to rerun. I've pushed `3d99406c` with two changes:

- Boundary-state copies now run separately from the varlen reduction. With the Dockerfile-pinned AMD Triton, offline gfx950 compilation improves from 18 aborts in 186 configurations to 186 successful compiles; another 96 specializations also compile.
- Final checkpoints now come directly from the scan, including after zero-dt padding. The 96 new checkpoint-consistency cases and 12 copy/stride cases pass on W7900D and 4090D.

The revision passes 402 related operator tests on W7900D and 766 on 4090D. Granite's 30-trial prefix test, exact token/logprob checks across six cache/chunking configurations, and all four sanitizer checks also pass on 4090D. The PR description has the results and test scope.

The five original split-state failures remain open for MI350X verification. When you have time, could you rerun those tests and default prefill, including Nemotron Nano and the Falcon-H1 `sampling_seed` case? I'd appreciate your help checking these on the original setup.

I'll coordinate the absolute-position alignment with #44076 when rebasing so both paths share one rule. Thanks again for your help.

@DQR-Happy  Thanks for the quick turnaround. I reran `3d99406c` on the same MI350X setup (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261013`, `--attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference`, AITER off, with #44197 and #44198 for the ROCm startup fixes):

1. **The compile abort is gone.** All three models start and serve with default chunked prefill.

2. **End to end** (`test_deterministic` `single`, `prefix` twice, `prefix --return-logprob`, `radix_cache`, plus a bitwise batch-size check: the same prompt in batches of 1 to 50, 1,275 responses, token IDs and logprobs compared exactly):

   | Model | default chunked prefill | `--chunked-prefill-size -1` |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Granite 4.0-H tiny | all pass | all pass |
   | Nemotron Nano 9B v2 | all pass | all pass |
   | Falcon-H1 7B | all pass | `prefix` 2/2/3/2 distinct outputs (twice), prefix logprobs differ; `single`, `radix_cache` and bitwise pass |

   So the Falcon-H1 case still differs, now only without chunked prefill: `prefix` sends prompts of different lengths together, and `test_deterministic` always sets a `sampling_seed` (temperature 0).

3. **`test_mamba_chunk_scan_split_boundary_state`** still fails on MI350X, less often: 1, 2 and 1 failures of 42 in three runs of that test alone, and 5 failures in the full run of the PR's tests (770 passed). The failing cases change from run to run; all are fp16 states (`state_dtype=torch.float16`) with `with_initial_state=False`, across most shapes (chunk 64/128/256; 1-3 splits). bf16 states no longer fail.

Happy to rerun again, or to run anything narrower that would help pin down the remaining split-state difference on this GPU.

I ran the Mamba GPU tests and the 30-trial Granite prefix reproduction on an RTX 4090; the results and a remaining cache-dependent logprob difference are in the description.

Hi @DQR-Happy. I tested this PR on AMD MI350X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.4, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261012`) with Granite 4.0-H tiny, Falcon-H1 7B and Nemotron Nano 9B v2, `--attention-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference`, triton everywhere. (On ROCm these models also need two small startup fixes, #44197 and #44198: `mamba.py` does not import the causal conv1d kernels on ROCm, and `ReLU2` has no ROCm path. Both were applied in both runs below.)

Same batch-size check as `test_deterministic --test-mode single`, but comparing every response's token IDs and log-probabilities with the batch-size-1 one (1,275 responses):

| Model | without the PR | with the PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Granite 4.0-H tiny | 359 / 1,275 token IDs, 99 log-probabilities identical | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Falcon-H1 7B | 397 / 99 | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| Nemotron Nano 9B v2 | 1,245 / 99 | 1,275 / 1,275 |

The PR's kernel test (`test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py`) passes on MI350X: 380 passed (16 of them fail without the PR).

`--test-mode prefix` (prompts of different lengths in one batch) improves a lot (Granite distinct outputs per group 1/106/9/6 -> 1/1/2/1) but is not fully clean. On our side that comes from chunked prefill: with `--chunked-prefill-size -1`, Granite and Nemotron-H pass every mode, log-probabilities included. Aligning the chunked-prefill split to `mamba_chunk_size` (as #44076 does for Gated DeltaNet) reduces the differences but does not remove them, and storing the SSM state in fp32 (`--mamba-ssm-dtype float32`) does not change them, so a split prompt still ends up slightly different from an unsplit one; we have not tracked that down yet. Falcon-H1 also differs without chunked prefill, but only when the request carries a `sampling_seed` (which `test_deterministic` always sends), even at temperature 0.

Thanks for the PR.

@aarnetalman Thanks for testing this on MI350X and narrowing down the remaining cases. I've pushed a follow-up for chunked prefill and cache reuse.

Alignment alone was not enough: a continuation could restart from a decode-produced checkpoint, and low-precision SSM caches rounded split and unsplit scans differently. The update uses canonical scan checkpoints, aligns splits by the absolute end position, and applies the same boundary rounding in both paths. It also keeps recurrent decode/verify states out of the prefill cache.

On W7900D I reproduced a mixed-batch difference with the original PR: 12 BF16 output elements differed for a 256-token request after a 31-token neighbor. Explicitly clearing the previous sequence's accumulator to positive zero before the local dot fixed that case. I cannot yet say whether this is the cause of the residual MI350X differences you saw.

The local coverage is:

| Platform | Tested revision and result |
| --- | --- |
| RTX 4090 D | Latest core: 1,004 GPU tests passed, 16 SM100-only cases skipped. Granite's 30-trial prefix test and exact token/logprob comparisons across split-prefill, cache and low-precision-state settings passed. |
| W7900D | Earlier follow-up: 438 operator tests, 960 Granite responses across five configurations, and 18 decode-cache reuse cases passed. Model runs needed separate RDNA startup/build adaptations. |
| Ascend 910B2C | Earlier follow-up: 24 zero-tolerance scan cases without initial states passed. Initial-state compilation and model startup remain blocked on that software stack; this is not full NPU validation. |

Only the 4090 D has run the final expanded core revision. The PR description now includes these boundaries and the measured 7.9% throughput cost on the fixed Granite workload. Separate NGRAM and FlashInfer issues are documented there too.
